맞다.gloss: to be right, to be correct

meanings.note: Used to confirm facts or answers.

meanings.en: to fit, to suit, to match
meanings.note: E.g., 사이즈가 맞다 ('the size fits').

examples.trans: Yes, that's my phone number.
These shoes fit my feet perfectly.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.text: 티 안 내려고 무지 애는 쓰시는데 저는 조금 알 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: She tries hard not to show it, yet I think I understand that feeling a little.

examples.text: 조금만 더 가면 금방 도착할 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: If we go just a little farther, we should arrive soon.

meanings.note: Used before adjectives or verbs.

examples.trans: Please give me a little more.
It's further away.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: With future or present-progressive verbs, means 'right away / in a moment'.
With past-tense verbs, means 'just now'.

examples.trans: I'll be right there.
I just arrived a moment ago.

examples.text: 조금만 더 가면 금방 도착할 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: If we go just a little farther, we should arrive soon.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 도착하다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (will arrive).

examples.text: 거의 아홉 시 넘었는데 빨리 찾아봐야 되는 거 아니에요?
examples.trans: It is almost past nine o'clock, shouldn't you find the way quickly?

examples.text: 거의 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (almost, nearly), we will get good results.
There are nine here.
Altogether, it is nine people.

meanings.note: Bound counter noun used with native Korean numbers (한 시, 두 시, 세 시, 네 시).

examples.trans: What time is it now?
The meeting starts at three o'clock.

examples.text: 이십 년 넘게 친구 설정으로 지냈는데 쉽진 않겠지.
examples.trans: You lived as friends for over twenty years, so changing that won't be easy.

examples.text: 거의 아홉 시 넘었는데 빨리 찾아봐야 되는 거 아니에요?
examples.trans: It is almost past nine o'clock, shouldn't you find the way quickly?

meanings.note: adverbial form of 빠르다 (to be fast)

examples.trans: Please get ready quickly.
Time goes by so fast.

examples.text: 거의 아홉 시 넘었는데 빨리 찾아봐야 되는 거 아니에요?
examples.trans: It is almost past nine o'clock, shouldn't you find the way quickly?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 찾아보다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (must look for).

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean word for telephone.

examples.trans: A phone call came.
I will hang up the phone.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

examples.text: 지금 여기가 전화가 잘 안 터져 가지고요.
examples.trans: Cell reception does not really get through out here right now.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 터지다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (get through (signal)).

meanings.en: to have, to possess, to take
meanings.note: Often shortened to 갖다.

examples.trans: I have an interest.
Please bring it (take it and come).
One moment please, let me swap the camera battery.
The topic of just a moment came up during this shoot.
One moment please, let me swap the camera battery.
The topic of battery came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Spoken contraction of bound noun 것; used in -(으)ㄴ/는 거예요 to ask or explain a situation.

examples.trans: Where are you going right now?
That is mine.

meanings.note: Native Korean word for a single day's span

examples.trans: How was your day today?
The day goes by really fast.

examples.text: 하루 종일 밥도 안 먹이고 이렇게 산길 헤매게 만들고요.
examples.trans: You haven't fed me all day and made me wander around this mountain trail.

examples.text: 가위바위보 해서 져서 내가 하루 종일 들고 다니는 걸로 찍혔잖아요.
examples.trans: I lost rock-paper-scissors and was already filmed carrying them all day.

meanings.note: Literal meaning: steamed rice.
By extension, refers to a meal in everyday expressions like 밥 먹다 ('to eat a meal').

examples.trans: Have you eaten?
Today's lunch is delicious.

meanings.note: Causative form of 먹다 ('to eat').

examples.trans: I feed the child a meal.
I fed the puppy a treat.

meanings.note: Adverbial form of 이렇다.
Used to emphasize degree.

examples.trans: You can do it like this.
Why is it so cold today?

examples.text: 하루 종일 밥도 안 먹이고 이렇게 산길 헤매게 만들고요.
examples.trans: You haven't fed me all day and made me wander around this mountain trail.

examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (getting dark and).
I'm always anxious before an exam.
I feel a bit uneasy when I'm alone.

meanings.en: to be dying of (hyperbolic emphasis in -아/어 죽겠다)

examples.trans: I'm starving to death.
It's so hot I feel like I'm going to die.

examples.text: 어제는 술 먹고 들이닥친 거고 오늘은 짐 들어 준 거잖아.
examples.trans: Yesterday he barged in drunk, and today he just carried my bags.

examples.trans: Shall we play rock-paper-scissors to carry each other's bags?

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: repeating an action or returning to a previous state

examples.trans: Please say that one more time.
I'll come back in a moment.

meanings.en: to hold, to carry in one's hand
meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb; 들고 가다 means 'to carry along'.

examples.trans: Please take your bag with you.
If it's heavy, I'll carry it.

examples.text: 우리 가위바위보 해서 서로 짐 들어 주기 할까요?
examples.trans: Shall we play rock-paper-scissors to carry each other's bags?

examples.text: 저 가위 낼게요. 안 내면 진 거, 가위바위보!
examples.trans: I am going to throw scissors. Lose if you don't throw—rock, paper, scissors!

examples.text: 저 가위 낼게요. 안 내면 진 거, 가위바위보!
examples.trans: I am going to throw scissors. Lose if you don't throw—rock, paper, scissors!

examples.text: 가위바위보 해서 져서 내가 하루 종일 들고 다니는 걸로 찍혔잖아요.
examples.trans: I lost rock-paper-scissors and was already filmed carrying them all day.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to go around, to attend, to commute
meanings.note: Indicates regular movement or carrying something around constantly.

examples.trans: I commute to the company.
I carry a bag around with me.

meanings.en: to get nicked, dented, or chipped
meanings.note: Passive form of 찍다 ('to strike/poke/stamp').
Used in 사진이 찍히다.

examples.trans: The car got a tiny nick.
The photo came out well.
If viewers criticize me, are you going to take responsibility, producer?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 욕먹다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (if I get criticized).

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.
If viewers criticize me, are you going to take responsibility, producer?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 책임지다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (take responsibility).

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
